description: The Rust orchestration spine: P1.2 persistence layer (sqlx SQLite Db + versioned migrations + repositories + AppConfig with schema_version), P1.3 secrets keystore (SecretStore trait + keyring-backed impl + in-memory/mock impl for CI-safe tests, resolving SecretRef handles with no raw-key getter), P1.4 SessionManager over the repos (create/list/rename/tag/delete conversations, append messages, assign personas, per-conversation route pins + privacy tags, plus the Section 7.5 per-conversation write lock), and P1.5 CoreEvent variants. Depends on FEAT-001 (domain models must exist). These crates all gain crates.io deps (sqlx, keyring, tokio, serde, uuid, chrono, thiserror, async-trait) so they are CI-authoritative per the arrangement FEAT-001 established.
steps: Read architecture.md Sections 7.2 (persistence: SQLite via sqlx, versioned migrations, tables conversations/messages/agent_personas/mcp_servers/providers/app_config, repositories), 7.5 (concurrency: per-conversation write lock), 9.1 (secrets: keyring, SecretRef, no raw key ever returned), 10.4 (schema_version). Read the FEAT-001 findings for the chosen workspace arrangement and the SecretRef definition decision.

P1.3 secrets crate: In crates/secrets/src/lib.rs define `SecretRef` (a stable string handle, serde-serializable, e.g. namespaced service+account id) and a `SecretStore` trait with methods to store a secret and receive a SecretRef, resolve a SecretRef to secret material ONLY for internal core use (return type must NOT be exposed via any public getter that could cross IPC; document this), and delete/rotate. CRITICAL: no method should return plaintext to callers outside the core's controlled use; the trait's resolve method is the single internal seam. Implement a `KeyringSecretStore` backed by the `keyring` crate (namespaced service id per Section 9.1). ALSO implement an `InMemorySecretStore` (behind a test/feature or always-available) so tests do NOT require a real OS keychain - headless Linux CI has no Secret Service and keyring tests would hang/fail. Add crates.io deps to crates/secrets/Cargo.toml (keyring, thiserror, serde) referencing [workspace.dependencies]. Add cargo tests: store then resolve a SecretRef round-trips (using InMemorySecretStore), AND a test asserting no public getter returns the plaintext key material (e.g. verify the SecretRef Debug/serde form contains only the handle, not the secret, and that there is no accessor exposing plaintext other than the documented internal resolve). Gate any keyring-backed test so it does not run on headless CI (e.g. #[ignore] or cfg), and rely on InMemory for the CI-run assertions.

P1.2 persistence crate: In crates/persistence/Cargo.toml add deps sqlx (features runtime-tokio + sqlite + macros or the offline query approach; prefer runtime-agnostic sqlite feature set that compiles without a live DB - use plain query() APIs, NOT the compile-time-checked query! macros, to avoid needing DATABASE_URL at build time), tokio, serde, serde_json, uuid, chrono, thiserror, plus a path dep on orchestrator-core for the domain models. In src/db.rs implement `Db` wrapping a sqlx SqlitePool with a constructor that opens a SQLite file (and a helper for a temp/in-memory DB for tests) and runs migrations at startup. Implement versioned migrations: either sqlx::migrate! with a migrations/ dir of numbered .sql files, or an explicit versioned migration runner that records applied version in a schema_version/meta table. Create tables conversations, messages, agent_personas, mcp_servers, providers, app_config per Section 7.2 (store complex fields like privacy_tags/enabled_tool_servers/content/route/usage/transport/extra as JSON TEXT columns via serde_json). In src/repositories.rs implement ConversationRepo, PersonaRepo, and repos for messages, mcp_servers, providers with typed CRUD (insert/get/list/update/delete) mapping rows to/from the FEAT-001 domain models. Secrets are NEVER stored here - only SecretRef handles (providers table stores api_key_ref as the SecretRef handle string). In src/config.rs implement AppConfig load/save with a schema_version field (Section 10.4) persisted to app_config, with forward-compatible load (unknown newer fields preserved where feasible).

P1.2 tests: add cargo tests covering migrations run cleanly against a fresh temp SQLite file, and CRUD round-trips for conversations, messages, personas, mcp_servers, providers (insert -> get -> update -> list -> delete), plus AppConfig save/load preserving schema_version. Use a temp-file or in-memory SQLite DB created in the test. These are the tasks.md acceptance for persistence.

P1.4 SessionManager in orchestrator-core: In crates/orchestrator-core/src/session.rs (alongside the models, or a session_manager.rs module) implement `SessionManager` holding the repos (via the persistence crate) - add a path dep on persistence and any needed async runtime (tokio) + async-trait if used, updating orchestrator-core/Cargo.toml. Methods: create_conversation, list_conversations, rename_conversation, set_conversation_tags (privacy tags), set_conversation_route (per-conversation pin), delete_conversation, append_message, assign_persona. Implement the Section 7.5 per-conversation write lock: a map of per-conversation async locks (e.g. Mutex keyed by conversation Uuid) so writes within one conversation are serialized while different conversations proceed in parallel. Document that reads are concurrent and cross-conversation writes are not blocked.

P1.5 CoreEvent in orchestrator-core/src/events.rs: replace the placeholder with a `CoreEvent` enum having exactly these variants (serde-tagged for the frontend, camelCase): message_delta, message_complete, message_error, conversation_updated, conversation_created, conversation_deleted, mcp_state_changed, mcp_error, permission_requested, providers_changed, personas_changed. Give each variant a reasonable display-safe payload (ids, deltas, statuses, rationales) referencing the domain models where appropriate; NEVER include secret material (Section 9.1/9.2 event hygiene). Add a scoped #[allow(dead_code)] with a 'wired in Phase 2+/consumed by tauri-app in FEAT-003' note ONLY on variants/fields not yet constructed, to keep clippy -D warnings clean.

P1.4 tests: add orchestrator-core cargo tests covering session lifecycle: create a conversation, append messages, assign a persona, and exercise the per-conversation write lock (e.g. concurrent appends to the same conversation are serialized and both persist; appends to different conversations can proceed without deadlock). Use an in-memory/temp SQLite Db from the persistence crate.

Update or remove the Phase 0 placeholder()/smoke tests in persistence, secrets, and orchestrator-core now that real APIs exist; keep providers/mcp-client/routing placeholders intact if orchestrator-core's smoke test still references them, or update that smoke test accordingly. Ensure no dangling references.

Author all files with LF line endings. Run cargo fmt over these crates. Because these crates require crates.io deps unreachable offline, they will NOT build in the sandbox - do NOT attempt network installs. Verify code is syntactically consistent as far as offline tooling allows, and record clearly in findings that persistence/secrets/orchestrator-core compilation + tests are DEFERRED TO CI (network). Ensure the CI workflow from FEAT-001 builds+tests+clippies these three crates explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: secrets crate defines SecretStore trait + KeyringSecretStore + InMemorySecretStore; SecretRef handles are returned/resolved; a test asserts no public getter returns plaintext key material; keyring-backed tests are gated so CI-run tests use the in-memory store and require no OS keychain.

persistence crate implements Db (sqlx SqlitePool) with versioned migrations creating conversations/messages/agent_personas/mcp_servers/providers/app_config tables, typed repositories with CRUD, and AppConfig load/save with schema_version; secrets are stored only as SecretRef handles.
orchestrator-core SessionManager implements create/list/rename/tag/route-pin/delete conversations, append messages, assign personas, with the Section 7.5 per-conversation write lock.
orchestrator-core CoreEvent enum defines exactly the eleven listed variants with display-safe (no-secret) payloads.

cargo tests exist for: persistence migrations + CRUD round-trips against a temp SQLite file; secrets store/resolve + no-plaintext-leak; orchestrator-core session lifecycle incl. per-conversation lock.
CI workflow builds+tests+clippies persistence, secrets, orchestrator-core explicitly; clippy -D warnings clean (dead_code allows scoped + annotated where unavoidable).
Files use LF line endings; what cannot build offline is documented as deferred-to-CI in findings.
verification: These three crates require crates.io deps and CANNOT be verified offline; primary verification is CI. Do NOT attempt network installs.
Offline: run `cargo fmt --check` on the changed crates if the toolchain allows formatting without dep resolution; record result.
Confirm the CI workflow contains explicit build+test+clippy(-D warnings) steps for persistence, secrets, and orchestrator-core.
Read through the secrets tests to confirm one test would FAIL if a plaintext getter were added (i.e. it meaningfully asserts non-exposure), and that keyring tests are gated off headless CI.
Read the persistence tests to confirm they run migrations then perform real insert/get/update/delete against a temp SQLite DB (not static asserts).
